items.question: What does our homeowners insurance cover?
items.answer:
Our comprehensive homeowners insurance (HO-3 policy) provides protection for:

DWELLING COVERAGE (Coverage A):
- Covers: Structure of your home, attached structures
- Amount: Based on replacement cost (not market value)
- Includes: Roof, walls, floors, built-in appliances, plumbing, electrical
- Typical coverage: $200,000 to $1,000,000+

OTHER STRUCTURES (Coverage B):
- Covers: Detached garage, shed, fence, pool, gazebo
- Amount: Typically 10% of dwelling coverage
- Example: $300K dwelling = $30K other structures

PERSONAL PROPERTY (Coverage C):
- Covers: Furniture, clothing, electronics, appliances
- Amount: Typically 50-70% of dwelling coverage
- Example: $300K dwelling = $150K-$210K personal property
- Special limits: Jewelry ($2,500), cash ($500), electronics ($5,000)
- Upgrade: Scheduled personal property for high-value items

LOSS OF USE (Coverage D):
- Covers: Hotel, meals, temporary housing during repairs
- Amount: Typically 20-30% of dwelling coverage
- Duration: Until home is livable or policy limit reached

PERSONAL LIABILITY (Coverage E):
- Covers: Injuries to others, damage to others' property
- Amount: $100K, $300K, or $500K standard (higher available)
- Includes: Legal defense costs
- Examples: Guest slips on stairs, your dog bites neighbor

MEDICAL PAYMENTS (Coverage F):
- Covers: Minor injuries to guests (no fault required)
- Amount: $1,000-$5,000
- Example: Guest cuts hand on broken glass

COVERED PERILS: Fire, lightning, wind, hail, theft, vandalism, water damage (sudden), falling objects, and 12+ other named perils.

items.question: What is NOT covered by standard homeowners insurance?
items.answer:
Standard homeowners insurance does NOT cover these common situations:

NATURAL DISASTERS (Require separate policies):
✗ Flood damage - Need separate flood insurance ($400-$2,000/year)
✗ Earthquake damage - Separate earthquake policy required
✗ Landslides and sinkholes (in most policies)
✗ Hurricane/named storm deductibles may apply (1-5% of dwelling)

MAINTENANCE AND WEAR:
✗ Gradual damage (slow roof leak developing over months)
✗ Mold from maintenance issues (covered if from sudden event)
✗ Pest damage (termites, rodents, insects)
✗ Wear and tear, deterioration, aging
✗ Mechanical breakdown of systems

WATER DAMAGE:
✗ Sewer backup (add rider for $50-100/year)
✗ Sump pump failure (add rider)
✗ Flood (needs separate flood insurance)
✓ Sudden water damage IS covered (burst pipe, appliance leak)

OTHER EXCLUSIONS:
✗ Intentional damage
✗ War, nuclear hazard, government action
✗ Power failure (unless caused by covered peril)
✗ Vacancy over 60 days
✗ Business activities (need business policy)
✗ Dog bites from "dangerous breeds" (some insurers)
✗ Trampolines and diving boards (some insurers)

HIGH-VALUE ITEMS (Limited coverage):
✗ Jewelry over $2,500 total
✗ Art and collectibles over $5,000
✗ Cash over $500
✗ Business equipment
SOLUTION: Add scheduled personal property rider

AVAILABLE ENDORSEMENTS to fill gaps:
- Water backup coverage: $50-100/year
- Scheduled personal property: Varies by value
- Home business: $200-500/year
- Equipment breakdown: $40-80/year
- Increased jewelry limit: $20-50/year per $1,000

items.question: What is replacement cost versus actual cash value coverage?
items.answer:
This is a crucial difference that affects how much you receive after a claim:

REPLACEMENT COST (RC) - RECOMMENDED:
What it means:
- Pays to replace/repair with new items of similar kind and quality
- NO deduction for depreciation
- You get what it costs to rebuild/replace TODAY

Example claim:
- 10-year-old roof damaged (original cost $15,000)
- Current replacement cost: $20,000
- RC policy pays: $20,000 (minus deductible)

Cost: 10-15% higher premium than ACV
Best for: Primary homes, newer properties

ACTUAL CASH VALUE (ACV):
What it means:
- Pays replacement cost MINUS depreciation
- Factors in age, condition, wear and tear
- Settlement is typically much lower

Same example:
- 10-year-old roof (50% depreciated)
- Replacement cost: $20,000
- Depreciation: -$10,000
- ACV policy pays: $10,000 (minus deductible)

Cost: Lower premium (10-15% less than RC)
Best for: Investment properties, vacation homes

OUR RECOMMENDATION:
Dwelling (home structure): REPLACEMENT COST
- Critical to rebuild your home properly
- Most lenders require this
- Guaranteed replacement cost available (pays over limit if costs rise)

Personal Property: REPLACEMENT COST
- Upgrade from standard ACV for ~$50/year
- Example: 5-year-old TV stolen
  * ACV: Pays depreciated value (~$200)
  * RC: Pays to buy new equivalent (~$600)

KEY CONSIDERATIONS:
- Replacement Cost Guarantee: Pays up to 125-150% of dwelling limit
- Extended Replacement Cost: Pays 25-50% over limit
- Helpful when construction costs spike after disasters
- All our standard policies include RC on dwelling
- Personal property RC is optional upgrade

items.question: How much homeowners insurance do I need?
items.answer:
Determining the right coverage amount is critical. Here's how we calculate it:

DWELLING COVERAGE (Most Important):
Based on REPLACEMENT COST, not market value or mortgage amount.

How we calculate:
1. Home square footage × Local rebuild cost per sq ft
2. Typical rebuild cost: $150-$300+ per sq ft
3. Factors: Materials, labor, architecture, features

Example:
- 2,500 sq ft home
- Local rebuild cost: $200/sq ft
- Recommended dwelling coverage: $500,000

Note: Market value ($400K) and mortgage ($300K) are irrelevant

OTHER COVERAGES (Auto-calculated from dwelling):
- Other Structures: 10% of dwelling ($50K)
- Personal Property: 50-70% of dwelling ($250-350K)
- Loss of Use: 20-30% of dwelling ($100-150K)

LIABILITY COVERAGE:
Recommended minimum: $300,000
Better protection: $500,000
Best: $1,000,000 (only ~$50 more per year)

Consider umbrella policy if:
- Net worth over $500K
- You own rental properties
- You have a pool, trampoline, or aggressive dog
- Teens drivers in household
- Cost: $200-400/year for $1-2M additional coverage

ADJUST COVERAGE FOR:
Increase if you have:
- High-end finishes (granite, hardwood, custom cabinets)
- Swimming pool or expensive landscaping
- Detached garage or workshop
- Home office with expensive equipment
- Valuable jewelry, art, or collectibles

Decrease factors:
- Basic finishes
- Smaller home
- Minimal landscaping
- No detached structures

TOOLS WE PROVIDE:
- Free replacement cost estimator (online or by phone)
- Annual coverage review reminder
- Automatic inflation protection (coverage increases 2-4% yearly)

WARNING SIGNS YOU'RE UNDERINSURED:
- Coverage hasn't been updated in 3+ years
- You've done major renovations
- Your coverage equals your mortgage amount
- Local construction costs have spiked

We'll review your coverage free annually to ensure adequate protection.

items.question: Do I need flood insurance?
items.answer:
Flood insurance is a separate policy from homeowners insurance. Here's what you need to know:

WHO NEEDS FLOOD INSURANCE:
High-risk areas (required by lenders):
- Special Flood Hazard Areas (SFHA / Zone A or V)
- 100-year flood plain
- Near rivers, lakes, coasts
- Mandatory if you have a mortgage

Moderate-to-low risk (strongly recommended):
- 25-30% of flood claims come from low-risk areas
- Flash floods can happen anywhere
- Even slight elevation changes matter

COVERAGE DETAILS:
Building Coverage:
- Maximum: $250,000 for dwelling
- Covers: Structure, foundation, electrical, plumbing, HVAC
- Cost: $400-$2,000/year (avg $700/year)

Contents Coverage:
- Maximum: $100,000 for personal property
- Separate from building coverage
- Must be purchased in addition
- Cost: $200-800/year additional

Deductibles:
- Options: $1,000 to $10,000
- Separate for building and contents
- Higher deductible = Lower premium

WHAT'S COVERED:
✓ Structure of home
✓ Electrical and plumbing systems
✓ HVAC and water heater
✓ Built-in appliances
✓ Personal belongings (if contents coverage purchased)
✓ Basement items (limited coverage)

WHAT'S NOT COVERED:
✗ Additional living expenses
✗ Swimming pools
✗ Landscaping
✗ Septic systems
✗ Wells
✗ Currency, precious metals

IMPORTANT NOTES:
- 30-day waiting period before coverage starts
- Buy before storm is named/forecasted
- Available through NFIP or private insurers
- We can quote and bind coverage

PRIVATE FLOOD vs NFIP:
NFIP (National Flood Insurance Program):
- Maximum $250K building / $100K contents
- Standard rates
- Government-backed

Private Flood Insurance:
- Higher limits available (up to $2-4M)
- Often cheaper in low-risk areas
- More coverage options
- We offer both - we'll quote best option

CHECK YOUR RISK:
- Free flood map check at www.floodsmart.gov
- Enter your address
- See your flood zone
- Call us for personalized quote: 1-800-INSURANCE

Even in low-risk areas, consider coverage:
- Just 1 inch of water causes $25,000 damage average
- Federal disaster aid is typically a loan (must repay)
- Flood insurance pays you to rebuild (don't repay)
